rows.notes: The generator itself (buildRandomRangeSet), not an assertion site. Counted in the population by the regex; excluded from the law tally.

rows.law: RangeSet(ranges) == fold of insert(contentsOf:) over the same ranges
rows.notes: Bulk construction equals incremental construction. differential-equivalence pairs NAMED variants (fast/reference); here the reference is a fold written in the test, so no source-only pairing exists.

rows.law: i in parent.indices[set] <=> set.contains(i); i in indices.removingSubranges(set) => !set.contains(i)
rows.notes: Membership biconditional between a subscript-selection and contains(). selection-subset/filter-subset state one direction at most.

rows.law: representation invariant: no empty range; adjacent ranges strictly ordered and disjoint
rows.notes: We HAVE the template and it cannot fire: it is annotation-only by design (@CheckProperty(.preservesInvariant)), and stdlib carries no annotation. Coverage exists, reach does not.

rows.law: Duration.seconds(d).components == (Int64(d), 0)
rows.notes: Scaled round-trip: project(construct(x)) == decompose(x). round-trip needs type symmetry (Double->Duration vs Duration->(Int64,Int64)) and does not pair these.

rows.law: Duration.milliseconds(d).components == (d/1000, d%1000 * 1e15)
rows.notes: Same shape at a different scale.

rows.law: Duration.microseconds(d).components == (d/1e6, d%1e6 * 1e12)

rows.law: Duration.nanoseconds(d).components == (d/1e9, d%1e9 * 1e9)
rows.notes: Same shape at a different scale.

rows.law: randomElement() is always a member; over 1000 draws every element appears
rows.notes: Two laws in one site. Membership is predicate-shaped; SURJECTIVITY over N draws is distributional and no template states it.

rows.law: [].randomElement() == nil
rows.notes: The empty-input edge; input-totality is exactly this.

rows.law: alphabet.elementsEqual(shuffled().sorted()) — shuffle preserves the multiset
rows.notes: A permutation invariant. normal-form is parse-print specific and does not apply.

rows.law: same LCRNG seed => identical draw sequence
rows.notes: Seeded determinism. Adjacent to the @ClockDeterministic claim but that admits async; this is RNG reproducibility.

rows.law: String(Character(s)) == s for s a SINGLE grapheme cluster — the String-side half of the Character retraction pair, plus scalar/representation checks
rows.template: LosslessStringConvertible (kit) for the Character-side half; none for the String-side retraction
rows.notes: CORRECTED 2026-07-30, was `ours-covers` via round-trip — and it also contradicted the roundtrip section, which had verdicted the same law `gap-with-witness`. BOTH were imprecise. `extension Character: LosslessStringConvertible` (Character.swift:195), so the kit runs the CHARACTER-side direction Character(String(describing:c)) == c, total. The test states the STRING-side direction String(Character(s)) == s, which is only true on single grapheme clusters and which nothing runs. Our own NormalFormTemplate doc already draws this distinction — 'a parse-print pair admits three laws, and they do NOT have the same truth conditions' — the adjudication simply failed to apply it. discover proposes ZERO suggestions citing Character.swift, so it is also a reach miss for the uncovered half.

rows.law: a.applying(b.difference(from:a)) == b; applied.applying(d.inverse()) == a
rows.notes: The textbook diff/patch inverse pair, plus inverse() as an involution.

rows.law: repeated .description on a bridged NSError yields the same value (no over-release)
rows.notes: REFUTABLE f(x)==f(x): see notes.md. Under ObjC bridging repeated observation is not trivially stable.

rows.law: as above, for a large struct payload
rows.notes: Same law, second layout.

rows.law: calling a stored closure 10x applies its effect 10x
rows.notes: Tests that InlineArray stores a closure callably. A counting check, not a quantified law.

rows.law: description round-trips (Value(String(describing:x)) == x) AND is the SHORTEST string that does so, for d and its 10 nextUp/nextDown neighbours
rows.template: LosslessStringConvertible (kit) for the round-trip half; none for shortness
rows.generator: nextUp/nextDown walk from a seed value
rows.notes: CORRECTED 2026-07-30, was `gap-in-reach` blaming initializerPairAdmissible's `guard label != "init"`. The kit RUNS the round-trip half as "LosslessStringConvertible.roundTrip", so relaxing that gate would have created a double-report, not closed a gap. `expectAccurateDescription` checks round-trip THEN shortness ("it makes no sense to check shortness if the result is inaccurate") — the shortness half is the real gap and no template states it.

rows.notes: Absorbing-state idempotence on an iterator. state-machine is scoped to view-model move carriers.

rows.law: after 20 appends a copy compares equal (value semantics) and nativeCapacity <= 40
rows.template: ValueSemantic (kit) for the copy half; none for the capacity bound
rows.notes: Two laws. Copy-independence is the kit's ValueSemantic. The capacity growth BOUND has no template and is the interesting half.

corrections.why: Both were filed against the init-label gate as a blocker to relax. PropertyLawKit already runs the law behind that gate, so relaxing it would have recreated the Strideable double-report fixed the same day. The genuine gap is the SHORTNESS half, which the kit does not cover.

Third site in one day resolved by LosslessStringConvertible, and the third mis-verdict about it — this one contradicted the roundtrip section, which had called the same law gap-with-witness. The kit runs one DIRECTION of the retraction pair; the test states the other, domain-restricted one. Direction and domain were both being elided.
